_note: The W14.8 pick gate's live record. `picks` is line -> era -> APPROVED seed, and it is what phase3_units_topdown_sheets.py draws as the green reference row; a cell belongs here only once the human has named a seed for it. `awaiting_seed_pick` is the gap that matters: in a re-roll round the human accepted the CELL ("agree, re-roll the others") without naming a seed, so the wording is settled but the pick is not, and the reference row cannot show it. The value is that round's first seed, purely so the round is identifiable; rebuild the line's sheet at those seeds to close one. It is empty when every cell in the roster has a named seed, which is the state the freeze scripts require.

5.why: e3 is the only img2img cell in the top-down roster: wording is exhausted on it (four rounds, sixteen seeds, every one running off the bottom edge) while e6 has held a self-contained segment since the first sweep, so e3 inherits e6's composition and the prompt repaints the material. e1 and e4 are txt2img re-rolls, and they are here because they were never re-rolled alongside e2/e3/e5 and still carry the defect those three were fixed for: every identity word in their cores was a height word, so the camera went to the vertical face. e1 rendered as a plank fence seen from the side and e4 as a sandbag stack tapering to a vanishing point.

6.why: e3 again, as txt2img with the long-line phrase removed from its core, to give the human an alternative to the img2img candidates. It failed harder: 43-57% bottom-edge bleed in all four, against 0.0% for the img2img set. Five rounds and twenty seeds across two opposed strategies puts this cell at the §8.3 rung-4 stop signal, and the cause is now understood to be the SUBJECT: a crenellated wall-walk is a pair of long parallel merlon rows flanking a corridor, and a long parallel line set triggers perspective by itself (cookbook §14), so no wording can remove what the subject is made of.
6.resolution: REJECTED by the human on the round's own criterion rather than on the bleed measurement: 'the 59x series is not a standalone field object'. Bottom-edge bleed and not-a-discrete-object are the same defect seen from two sides — a segment that runs off the frame has no visible end, and a barrier without visible ends reads as terrain the field is made of rather than a thing standing on it (review-brief-units-topdown.md, discrete object with visible ends). The cell ships as round 5's img2img s491, which inherits e6's self-contained composition; the subject question is therefore closed without a subject change.

barrier_render_axis._note: Measured on the APPROVED shield_wall sprites (PCA long axis of the foreground mask; 0 deg = the segment lies left-to-right, 90 deg = top-to-bottom, screen y down). The human's ruling is that every era reads TOP-TO-BOTTOM on the field, across the lane, and that the view supplies the rotation rather than the renderer — so the render axis is per-asset data the view needs, not a defect. Four of six already render top-to-bottom and rotate by nothing. Two do not, and they are the open item: e5's is a clean lossless 90 deg, but e2 renders diagonally and needs ~44 deg, which resamples the sprite and swings its shading with it. Whether e2 is rotated, re-rolled onto the axis, or accepted diagonal is a human call; nothing here decides it.
